summary:
ORBIT: Interactive Space Mission Simulator

ORBIT is an educational simulator that allows users to experience the main stages of a lunar space mission through engineering, planning, and resource management decisions. The project guides participants from selecting a mission objective and designing a spacecraft with components limited by budget and mass, to launch, Earth-Moon transit, lunar approach, descent, and surface exploration.

Throughout the mission, users must monitor systems such as power, communications, life support, and navigation, respond to risky situations, and make decisions that affect the outcome. At the end, they receive a score, a record of their decisions, and a comparison with real-world data.

ORBIT addresses the challenge by turning complex space exploration concepts into an interactive, hands-on experience. It is important because it brings aerospace science and engineering closer to students and future professionals, encourages critical thinking, and demonstrates how every decision can influence the success of a mission.
details:
Project Details – ORBIT

ORBIT is an educational lunar mission simulator designed to help users understand and experience the challenges of planning, developing, and executing a space mission. Its gameplay is organized into different stages, allowing participants to make decisions and observe how those decisions influence the progress and outcome of the mission.

The experience begins with selecting the mission objective, lunar landing location, and launch vehicle. Participants then design their spacecraft by selecting eight components while managing a budget of 130 credits and respecting the launch vehicle's maximum mass limit. Once the spacecraft is ready, they must perform system checks, initiate the launch, manage the Earth-to-Moon transit, correct the trajectory, complete the lunar approach, and perform the landing. Finally, they carry out activities on the lunar surface, such as collecting samples and taking photographs, before returning and reviewing the final mission report.

Throughout the mission, users must monitor essential systems such as power, communications, navigation, and life support, while responding to potential risks and technical failures. The simulator includes monitoring and control tools such as a Heads-Up Display (HUD), radio communications, and system consoles including EPS, COMM, GNC, ECLSS, and PROC. At the end, users receive a score out of 100, a record of their decisions and consequences, and a comparison with real-world data.

Technologies Used: The project uses Unity as its development engine to build the simulator's interactive experience. GitHub is also used as the project's repository and code management platform, supporting version control, code organization, and collaboration among team members.

ORBIT offers several educational benefits, including practical learning of aerospace concepts, critical thinking, problem-solving, and efficient resource management. Its intended impact is to make aerospace engineering and space exploration more accessible to students and future professionals through an engaging, interactive learning experience.

ORBIT's creativity lies in combining spacecraft engineering, mission planning, resource management, and performance evaluation into a single experience. Rather than simply presenting theoretical information, it allows users to learn through decisions, challenges, and their consequences.

During its design, the team considered mission feasibility, budget and mass limitations, available energy, communications, life-support systems, navigation, landing risks, and the need to provide clear and understandable feedback to users.
